stem: At what age is it generally appropriate to begin 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring in a child with hypertension?

options.text: From birth if the child is hypertensive

explanation: Older than 5 or 6 years is the usual age at which a child can reliably tolerate and cooperate with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because children younger than this often struggle to keep the cuff on and complete the monitoring period.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because neonates are not generally able to tolerate or cooperate with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the test can be used in younger school-age children who can comply with wearing the device.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because age 12 is not the threshold; monitoring may be appropriate well before adolescence.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because birth is far too early for routine 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.

source.hint: Think about the developmental stage at which a child can realistically cooperate with wearing a cuff all day.
